topics.title: 3.1.1 Understanding the nature and purpose of business

outcomes.text: Explain why businesses exist and the objectives they set: profit, growth, survival, cash flow, social and ethical aims.
Explain how a mission relates to objectives and why businesses set objectives.
Measure profit and explain its importance, using revenue, fixed costs, variable costs and total costs.

topics.title: 3.1.2 Understanding different business forms

outcomes.text: Explain why owners choose, or change, a business form such as sole trader, private or public limited company, public sector, non-profit or social enterprise.
Compare limited and unlimited liability, share capital, market capitalisation and dividends across forms.
Describe the role of shareholders and why they invest.
Explain what influences share price and why share price changes matter.
Explain how ownership affects a firm's mission and objectives.

topics.title: 3.1.3 Understanding that businesses operate within an external environment

outcomes.text: Explain how competition, market conditions, incomes, interest rates, demographics, environmental issues and fair trade affect costs and demand.

topics.title: 3.2.1 Understanding management, leadership and decision making

outcomes.text: Distinguish management from leadership.
Describe leadership styles (autocratic, paternalistic, democratic, laissez-faire) and what influences them, including the Tannenbaum Schmidt continuum.
Judge how effective different management and leadership styles are.

topics.title: 3.2.2 Understanding management decision making

outcomes.text: Compare data-based (scientific) decision making with intuition, including reading decision trees and working out expected value and net gain.
Weigh risk, reward, uncertainty and opportunity cost in decisions, and the value of decision trees.
Explain how mission, objectives, ethics, the external environment and resource limits influence decisions.

topics.title: 3.2.3 Understanding the role and importance of stakeholders

outcomes.text: Explain why stakeholder needs must be considered in decisions, and use stakeholder mapping by power and interest.
Describe how stakeholder needs can overlap or conflict.
Explain how to manage relationships with different stakeholders through communication and consultation.

topics.title: 3.3.1 Setting marketing objectives

outcomes.text: Explain the value of marketing objectives such as sales volume and value, market size, growth, market share and brand loyalty.

topics.title: 3.3.2 Understanding markets and customers

outcomes.text: Explain the value of primary and secondary, qualitative and quantitative, marketing research.
Calculate market and sales growth, market share and market size.
Explain the value of random, stratified and quota sampling.
Interpret marketing data, including correlation and its strength, confidence intervals and extrapolation.
Interpret price and income elasticity of demand and analyse how price and income changes affect revenue.
Explain why elasticity matters to marketing decision makers.
Explain how data is used in marketing decisions and planning.

topics.title: 3.3.3 Making marketing decisions: segmentation, targeting, positioning

outcomes.text: Explain the process and value of segmenting a market by demographic, geographic, income or behavioural factors, then targeting and positioning.
Explain what influences the choice of target market and positioning, including niche versus mass marketing and market mapping.

topics.title: 3.3.4 Making marketing decisions: using the marketing mix

outcomes.text: Describe the 7Ps of the marketing mix and what influences changes to each, for goods and services, industrial and consumer.
Explain product decisions: portfolio analysis and the Boston Matrix, the product life cycle with extension strategies, and new product development.
Explain pricing decisions, including penetration and price skimming.
Explain promotional decisions, including branding, social media and viral marketing.
Explain distribution decisions, including multi-channel distribution.
Explain decisions on people, process and physical environment.
Explain what makes an integrated marketing mix work: product life cycle position, Boston Matrix, product type, objectives, target market, competition and positioning.
Explain the value of digital marketing and e-commerce.

topics.title: 3.4.1 Setting operational objectives

outcomes.text: Explain the value of operational objectives: costs, quality, speed of response, flexibility, environmental aims and added value.

topics.title: 3.4.2 Analysing operational performance

outcomes.text: Calculate and use labour productivity, unit costs, capacity and capacity utilisation in operational decisions.

topics.title: 3.4.3 Making operational decisions to improve performance: increasing efficiency and productivity

outcomes.text: Explain the importance of capacity and how to use it efficiently.
Explain how to raise efficiency and labour productivity, and why that can be difficult.
Explain the benefits and difficulties of lean production, including Just in Time versus Just in Case.
Choose the best mix of resources, comparing labour-intensive and capital-intensive processes.
Explain how technology can improve operational efficiency.

topics.title: 3.4.4 Making operational decisions to improve performance: improving quality

outcomes.text: Describe methods of improving quality, including quality assurance versus quality control.
Explain the benefits and difficulties of improving quality.
Explain the consequences of poor quality.

topics.title: 3.4.5 Making operational decisions to improve performance: managing inventory and supply chains

outcomes.text: Explain how to match supply to demand using outsourcing, temporary or part-time staff and producing to order.
Explain what influences the amount of inventory held, including inventory control charts, lead time, re-order levels, buffer stock and re-order quantity.
Explain what influences the choice of suppliers.
Explain how to manage the supply chain efficiently and why this is valuable.
Explain the value of outsourcing.

topics.title: 3.5.1 Setting financial objectives

outcomes.text: Explain the value of financial objectives: return on investment, revenue, cost and profit aims, and cash flow aims.
Distinguish cash flow from profit.
Distinguish gross profit, operating profit and profit for the year.

topics.title: 3.5.2 Analysing financial performance

outcomes.text: Build and analyse budgets and cash flow forecasts, including variance analysis with adverse and favourable variances.
Explain the value of budgeting.
Build and interpret break-even charts: break-even output, margin of safety, contribution per unit and total contribution.
Show on a break-even chart how changes in price, output and cost have an effect.
Explain the value of break-even analysis.
Analyse profitability using gross profit, operating profit and profit for the year margins.
Analyse the timing of cash inflows and outflows, including payables and receivables.
Explain how data supports financial decisions and planning.

topics.title: 3.5.3 Making financial decisions: sources of finance

outcomes.text: Describe internal and external sources of finance: debt factoring, overdrafts, retained profit, share capital, loans, venture capital and crowd funding.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of different sources for short- and long-term needs.

topics.title: 3.5.4 Making financial decisions: improving cash flow and profits

outcomes.text: Assess ways of improving cash flow.
Assess ways of improving profits and profitability.
Explain the difficulties of improving cash flow and profit.

topics.title: 3.6.1 Setting human resource objectives

outcomes.text: Explain the value of HR objectives: engagement, talent development, training, diversity, shared values, and the number, skills and location of staff.
Describe methods of achieving HR objectives, including soft and hard HRM approaches.

topics.title: 3.6.2 Analysing human resource performance

outcomes.text: Calculate and interpret labour turnover, labour productivity, employee costs as a share of turnover and labour cost per unit.
Explain how data supports HR decisions and planning.

topics.title: 3.6.3 Making human resource decisions: improving organisational design and managing the human resource flow

outcomes.text: Describe functional, product-based, regional and matrix organisational structures.
Explain what influences organisational design: authority, span, hierarchy, delegation, centralisation and decentralisation.
Explain the value of changing organisational design.
Explain how managing HR flow (planning, recruitment, training, redeployment, redundancy) helps meet HR objectives.

topics.title: 3.6.4 Making human resource decisions: improving motivation and engagement

outcomes.text: Explain the benefits of motivated and engaged employees, using the theories of Taylor, Maslow and Herzberg.
Describe financial methods (piece rate, commission, salary, performance-related pay) and non-financial methods (empowerment, teamwork, flexible working, job enrichment, job rotation) of motivation.
Judge what influences the choice and effectiveness of financial and non-financial methods.

topics.title: 3.6.5 Making human resource decisions: improving employer-employee relations

outcomes.text: Explain what influences how far employees are involved in decisions, including trade unions and works councils.
Explain how to manage and improve employer-employee communication and relations.
Explain the value of good employer-employee relations.

units.title: 3.7 Analysing the strategic position of a business

topics.title: 3.7.1 Mission, corporate objectives, functional objectives and strategy

outcomes.text: Explain the influences on a business's mission.
Explain internal and external influences on corporate objectives, including short-termism and ownership.
Explain the links between mission, corporate objectives and strategy, and the difference between strategy and tactics.
Explain how strategic decisions affect functional decisions and what influences functional objectives.
Explain the value of SWOT analysis.

topics.title: 3.7.2 Analysing the existing internal position of a business to assess strengths and weaknesses: financial ratio analysis

outcomes.text: Assess financial performance from balance sheets, income statements and ratios: ROCE, current ratio, gearing, payables days, receivables days and inventory turnover.
Explain the value of ratios when assessing performance over time or against other businesses.

topics.title: 3.7.3 Analysing the existing internal position of a business to assess strengths and weaknesses: overall performance

outcomes.text: Analyse operations, HR and marketing data over time or against rivals to find strengths and weaknesses.
Explain the importance of core competences.
Assess short- and long-term performance.
Explain the value of different measures of performance, including Elkington's Triple Bottom Line.

topics.title: 3.7.4 Analysing the external environment to assess opportunities and threats: political and legal change

outcomes.text: Explain how changes in competition, labour market and environmental law affect strategic and functional decisions.
Explain the impact of government policy on enterprise, regulators, infrastructure, the environment and international trade.

topics.title: 3.7.5 Analysing the external environment to assess opportunities and threats: economic change

outcomes.text: Explain how UK and global changes in GDP, taxation, exchange rates, inflation, fiscal and monetary policy, and open trade versus protectionism affect decisions.
Interpret economic data for the UK and globally and consider its implications for business.

topics.title: 3.7.6 Analysing the external environment to assess opportunities and threats: social and technological

outcomes.text: Explain how demographic change, migration, changing lifestyles and buying behaviour, and online growth affect decisions.
Explain corporate social responsibility: arguments for and against, stakeholder versus shareholder views, and Carroll's pyramid.
Explain how technological change affects functional areas and strategy.
Explain the pressures for socially responsible behaviour.

topics.title: 3.7.7 Analysing the external environment to assess opportunities and threats: the competitive environment

outcomes.text: Use Porter's five forces (entry threat, buyer power, supplier power, rivalry, substitutes), explain why they change and what they mean for decisions and profits.
Explain how the five forces shape competitive strategy.

topics.title: 3.7.8 Analysing strategic options: investment appraisal

outcomes.text: Calculate and interpret payback, average rate of return and net present value.
Explain the factors that influence investment decisions: criteria, non-financial factors, risk and uncertainty.

topics.title: 3.8.1 Strategic direction: choosing which markets to compete in and what products to offer

outcomes.text: Explain what influences the choice of markets and products, using the Ansoff matrix: penetration, market development, new product development and diversification.
Explain why options for strategic direction are chosen and how valuable they are.

topics.title: 3.8.2 Strategic positioning: choosing how to compete

outcomes.text: Explain how to compete on benefits and price using Porter's low cost, differentiation and focus strategies.
Explain what influences the choice of positioning strategy and the value of each.
Explain the benefits of competitive advantage.
Explain the difficulties of maintaining competitive advantage.

units.title: 3.9 Strategic methods: how to pursue strategies

topics.title: 3.9.1 Assessing a change in scale

outcomes.text: Explain why businesses grow or retrench, and the difference between organic and external growth.
Manage issues of growth and retrenchment: economies of scale and scope, diseconomies, synergy and overtrading.
Explain how growth or retrenchment affects the functional areas.
Assess methods of growth (mergers, takeovers, ventures, franchising) and types (vertical, horizontal, conglomerate integration).

topics.title: 3.9.2 Assessing innovation

outcomes.text: Explain pressures for innovation and the value of product and process innovation.
Describe ways to become innovative: Kaizen, R&D, intrapreneurship and benchmarking.
Explain how patents and copyrights protect innovation and intellectual property.
Explain how an innovation strategy affects the functional areas.

topics.title: 3.9.3 Assessing globalisation and internationalisation

outcomes.text: Explain the reasons for greater globalisation and its importance, including emerging economies.
Explain reasons for targeting and trading with international markets, and factors making them attractive.
Explain why firms produce and source abroad, including off-shoring and re-shoring.
Compare ways of entering international markets: export, licensing, alliances and direct investment, including multinationals.
Explain influences on buying, selling and producing abroad.
Explain how to manage international business, balancing local responsiveness and cost reduction.

topics.title: 3.9.4 Assessing greater use of digital technology

outcomes.text: Explain the pressures to adopt digital technology such as automation, e-commerce, big data and data mining.
Explain the value of digital technology.

topics.title: 3.10.1 Managing change

outcomes.text: Explain causes of and pressures for change, and types: internal, external, incremental and disruptive, using Lewin's force field analysis.
Explain the value of change.
Explain the value of a flexible organisation: restructuring, delayering, flexible contracts, organic versus mechanistic structures.
Explain the value of managing information and knowledge.
Explain barriers to change, using Kotter and Schlesinger's four reasons for resistance.
Explain how to overcome barriers using Kotter and Schlesinger's six approaches.

topics.title: 3.10.2 Managing organisational culture

outcomes.text: Explain the importance of organisational culture, using Handy's task, role, power and person cultures.
Explain the influences on organisational culture.
Explain the reasons for and problems of changing culture.

topics.title: 3.10.3 Managing strategic implementation

outcomes.text: Explain how to implement strategy effectively, including the value of leadership and communication.
Explain the importance of organisational structure in implementing strategy.
Use network analysis: read and amend network diagrams, find the critical path and total float.

topics.title: 3.10.4 Problems with strategy and why strategies fail

outcomes.text: Explain the difficulties of strategic decision making and implementation.
Distinguish planned from emergent strategy.
Explain the reasons for strategic drift.
Evaluate strategic performance.
Explain the value of strategic planning.
Explain the value of contingency planning and crisis management.
